prize_parts.citation: for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases by evolved deaminases without double-strand breaks
for the conception and demonstration of targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional molecules that recruit the ubiquitin-proteasome system

statement.case_for: I keep the same configuration after the full round-1 exchange, and I reach it by asking of each part what exactly was discovered, by whom, and when. Base editing: the discovery is the coupling of a deaminase to a catalytically impaired Cas protein so that a defined base is chemically converted without a double-strand break or donor template, followed by the evolution of an adenine deaminase that acts on DNA, which no natural enzyme did. That is a designed nucleobase reaction with a quantitative mechanism, replicated in very many laboratories and now in patients. Targeted protein degradation: the discovery is the 2001 demonstration that a bifunctional small molecule can enforce proximity between a target and an E3 ligase so that the cell removes a protein that has no active site to inhibit, with the ternary-complex energetics since measured and independently confirmed. In both cases a designed molecular recognition event gave a capability that did not exist, and the generative consequences are large. The union of Liu, Crews and Deshaies is exactly three people, and each part can be explained to a broad audience in one sentence.
statement.case_against: Round 1 sharpened my doubts rather than removing them. For B024, Liu alone excludes Komor and Gaudelli, whose first-author papers are the decisive experiments and whose evolved TadA deaminase is the clearest new chemistry in the field; the citation can carry their contribution through its wording about evolved deaminases, but it cannot name them, and I regard that as a real cost, not a technicality. The Kondo and Nishida priority question is also not closed from the record I have. For B009, no PROTAC is approved, Somfai and Sparr argue that the cereblon glue lineage (Handa) is on firmer ground, and Chabes doubts the evidence is ready. If the committee concludes that the Liu-only credit is untenable, the right fallback is B024 as the whole prize with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, not a weaker second part.

responses.point: Somfai holds B003 first, accepts B024 with Liu alone as a second part, but says the new chemistry in base editing is mainly protein engineering and directed evolution on top of CRISPR, and that B009 splits into PROTAC and glue lineages that three names merge awkwardly.
responses.response: Your distinction between old deamination chemistry and the new evolved deaminase and editor architecture is the one I would put into the citation, which is why I now say 'evolved deaminases' in the B024 wording; directed evolution that creates a reaction no enzyme performed on DNA is chemistry, and the double-strand-break-free outcome is a different mechanism from the 2020 prize. I also owe you a correction: my round-1 file proposes Liu alone, not the trio, so the choice you set me, trio as the whole prize or Liu as a second part, is open to me and I choose the second part. On B009 I accept that PROTAC and glue histories are different, which is why I credit only the heterobifunctional concept (Crews, Deshaies) and do not try to carry Handa. I do not agree that B003 should displace B009 as a partner: after the 2010 prize and the Kosugi precursor I read C-N coupling as the stronger extension of a recognised principle, which keeps it as my second alternative.

responses.point: Chabes proposes B024 as the whole prize for Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, argues that Gaudelli's evolved adenine deaminase is the strongest evidence of real chemistry, and says PROTAC evidence is not ready because no drug is approved and credit is spread across two lineages.
responses.response: I agree that the evolved TadA is the clearest new chemistry, and that is the strongest argument against my own Liu-only credit; I take it seriously, and I would move to your trio as a single-part prize if the committee finds Liu alone indefensible. I still prefer the two-part form because the question for B009 is the 2001 concept and its mechanistic validation, which does not depend on an approved drug any more than the 1990s prizes in enzyme and receptor chemistry depended on a marketed product. I also note that you said you would accept a two-name or single-name version of B024, and on Target-AID I share your uncertainty: I want the priority record checked, but a different architecture reported at about the same time argues for the citation wording, not for replacing Liu.

responses.point: Sparr argues that ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a physical-chemical concept (pKa-tuned charge, bilayer to non-bilayer phase behaviour), says her read of my ranking was that I treat B013 as application, and presses for explicit reasoning on why a first-author postdoc should be a laureate in a PI-led programme.
responses.response: I accept your correction that the endosomal-escape mechanism is phase-behaviour physics, and that is why B013 is my first alternative; my low opening rank reflected attribution across Vancouver, Inex and MIT and the 2023 Medicine overlap, not doubt about the chemistry. If the committee wants a mature, clinically validated part, B013 is the one I would swap in, but I still cannot cut it to three names without choosing between the ionizable lipid and the formulation process. On trainees, your question is the right test and my answer is conditional: a first author is a laureate when the decisive conceptual step is theirs, and for base editing I judge the concept to be Liu's while granting that Gaudelli's deaminase evolution is a strong exception case.

responses.point: Aili would fall back on the single-part trio of Liu, Komor and Gaudelli if the Liu-only credit proves indefensible, and anchors the degradation citation on the 2001 Crews-Deshaies concept with wording that acknowledges the glue branch.
responses.response: We agree on the structure and on the fallback, so the remaining question is who decides it. My test is whether a citation that speaks of evolved deaminases can fairly carry Komor and Gaudelli's work without naming them; if colleagues in the final ballot judge it cannot, I would support the trio as one part. I would not add a sentence on the glue branch to the B009 citation, because that is the merging of two histories that Brzezinski warned against; the glue lineage deserves its own discussion in a later year.

uncertainties: Whether Liu alone is defensible for base editing, or whether the evolved-deaminase chemistry makes Komor and Gaudelli necessary laureates, in which case B024 must stand alone.
The Target-AID priority record for Kondo and Nishida against Komor 2016 and Gaudelli 2017, which I cannot settle from the shortlist and which may change the wording more than the names.
Whether the 2001 PROTAC concept and mechanism can carry a prize before any PROTAC drug is approved, or whether Handa and the cereblon glue lineage is the mature core.
Whether a pairing of base editing and degradation reads as a coherent prize on programmable chemical control of biomolecules or only a loose shared theme.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name: none is at Lund University or a collaborator of mine. In round 1 I chaired the discussion and my configuration was counted among the four B024 plus B009 proposals, so I note that the chair's summary does not weigh my vote above any other member's. Somfai and Sparr are Lund colleagues, which is not a conflict for any shortlisted candidate. Round 1 left no recusal request, and I have none to add.
